full_judgment:
4. In the writ petition it was contended that the land measuring about 4.10 acres situated within former Dacca district at present Gazipur under P.S. Gazipur, Mouza-Mohona Bhabanipur, J.L. No. 3,B, Khatian No.669, C.S. Plot No.1422 (hereinafter referred to as case land) belonged to Bhawal C.W. Estate. (shortly as Bhawal State). 

 7. The Bhawal Court of Estate on granting settlement to the mother of the writ petitioner opened a khatian for the case land being khatian No. 669 of Mouza Mohona Bhabanipur, J.L. No. 3 in her name and realized rents etc. for the case land starting from the year 1346 B.S & realized rent up to the year 1361 B.S. 

 14. In the said order of respondent No.3 dated 07.07.2003 a direction was given to correct the record of the case land in the schedule to the effect that, P.S. Joydevpur, Mouza Mohona Bhabanipur, Khatian No. B/669, C.S Dag No. 1422 and R.S Dag No. 3826. area of land 4.10 acre. But in the said schedule R.S dag was wrongly quoted as 3826 instead of 8351, 8354, 8356 and 8358. As per R.S map the R.S plot of the case land should have been 8351, 8354, 8356 and '8358 corresponding to C.S Plot No. 1422. 

 20. It was also contended that the R. S. record of right has been finally published by operation of section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act therefore, the said khatian became a piece of evidence which has got the presumptive value of correctness within the meaning of section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, therefore, without rebut-ting the same by any legal evidence in a competent Court the order of mutation incorporating the R.S. plot numbers in respect of mutating the name of the writ petitioner cannot be done by the collector. As such the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) righty rejected the application of the writ petitioner in accordance with law. 

 "One important thing is required to be noticed in the case which is when title suit No.772 of 1981 was instituted the R.S. operation was not started. As such the mother of the petitioner instituted the suit upon incorporating the C.S. khatian and plot number. As such the decree was also passed on the basis of the C.S. plot number. The said CS. Plot No.1422 covering 4.10 acres of land has been subsequently renumbered as same R.S. Plots. Fact remains that the petitioner though mother got the decree on C.S. plot No. 1422 as such he is entitled to get his name mutated on the plots which arose out of the said C.S. plot. The decree passed by a civil Court covering C.S. plot No. 1422 having not been varied or set aside in any higher forum the petitioners decree cannot be frustrated."
